links.passage: Fertigation boosts production by 11–40% and improves fertilizer usage efficiency by 20–60% (NCPAH 2001).
supporting_passages: Fertigation has become more popular with the advent of methods such as sprinklers and drip irrigation.
Various crops receive the same quantity of nutrients at various times using a pooled drip irrigation technique called drip fertigation.
links.inference_note: The section frames fertigation as delivered through drip irrigation (drip fertigation), so the production boost attributed to fertigation is read as fertigation through drip lines.
reference_entries: NCPAH. 2001. National committee on plasticulture applications in horticulture. Progress report 2001. Ministry Of Agriculture, Gol, New Delhi.

links.passage: In greater yam, fertigation of N-P2O5-K2O @ 100-60-100 kg ha−1 resulted in a higher tuber yield of 34.2 t ha−1 (Nedunchezhiyan et al. 2023).
supporting_passages: In elephant foot yam, a higher corm yield (34.3 t ha−1) was obtained with the application of N-K2O @120–120 kg ha−1 through drip fertigation (Nedunchezhiyan 2017).
links.inference_note: The adjacent sentence names drip fertigation as the delivery method for these tuber-crop fertigation results, so the yield gain is attributed to fertigation through drip.
reference_entries: Nedunchezhiyan, M., K. Pati, V. B. S. Chauhan, K. H. Gowda, R. Arutselvan, G. Suja, and G. Byju. 2023. Climate resilient technologies for sustainable production of root and tuber crops. Journal of Root Crops 49 (1):3–10.
